From Hassela Press Release
March 25, 1998

On Monday, Scottish motorists were tested for illegal drugs for the first time as part of a Government crackdown on drugs driving. The trial were carried out by four police forces in a pilot scheme of field trials on new scientific equipment.

A total of 5,000 drivers in Cleveland, Lancashire, Strathclyde and Sussex will be stopped over a three-week period and asked to volunteer for the tests, being used in Britain for the first time.

The drivers are being tested with a device called Drugwipe, a pen-type swab wiped across the forehead.

Four different versions which can test for cannabis, cocaine, opiates or amphetamines are being used. Separate trial are planned for another device that tests for drugs thorugh saliva.

The test stick can identify a variety of drugs in under one minute. It detects the four major drug groups- cannabis, cocaine, opiates and amphetamines, including Ecstasy. It detects particles 1,000 times smaller than anything visible to the eye. It detects the drugs from sweat or saliva. It can also detect drugs on hard surfaces and clothing. It is already used successfully by police and Customs officers in Germany and Canada and by the FBI in the US.

There are only about 3,000 successful prosecutions a year in the UK for driving under the influence of drugs but 100,000 for drink-driving.
